ordered_diagnoses: Liver Metastasis from Other Primary Site

facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin
A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin

concepts.why: The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver, epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia, and diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E support this diagnosis.

The presence of epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments, as well as diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E, support this diagnosis.
The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver and elevated liver enzymes support this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for HCC.
The presence of a liver mass could be consistent with FNH, although the immunohistochemical staining results and the presence of epithelioid tumor cells are not typical for FNH.
The presence of a liver mass could be consistent with hemangioma, although the immunohistochemical staining results and the presence of epithelioid tumor cells are not typical for hemangioma.

concepts.preferred_label: Liver Metastasis from Other Primary Site
concepts.why: The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver could be consistent with liver metastasis from another primary site, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for this diagnosis.
The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver and elevated liver enzymes support this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for ICC.

The presence of a liver mass could be consistent with hepatic adenoma, although the immunohistochemical staining results and the presence of epithelioid tumor cells are not typical for hepatic adenoma.

rationales.F09: Multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver suggest a malignant process, which could be primary or metastatic.
rationales.F10: Epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments are characteristic of melanoma.
rationales.F11: Diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E is highly suggestive of melanoma.
rationales.F12: Negativity for cytokeratin helps to rule out carcinomas, including hepatocellular carcinoma and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
